mod_group_id=io.github.julianperge.modular_planters
---
plugins {
    id 'java-library'
    id 'net.neoforged.moddev' version '2.0.141'
    id 'idea'
}

tasks.named('wrapper', Wrapper).configure {
    distributionType = Wrapper.DistributionType.BIN
}

version = mod_version
group = mod_group_id

repositories {
    maven {
        url "https://www.cursemaven.com"
        content {
            includeGroup "curse.maven"
        }
    }
}

base {
    archivesName = mod_id
}

java.toolchain.languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)

neoForge {
    version = project.neo_version

    runs {
        client {
            client()
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        server {
            server()
            programArgument '--nogui'
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        gameTestServer {
            type = "gameTestServer"
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        data {
            clientData()
            programArguments.addAll '--mod', project.mod_id, '--all', '--output', file('src/generated/resources/').getAbsolutePath(), '--existing', file('src/main/resources/').getAbsolutePath()
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        configureEach {
            systemProperty 'forge.logging.markers', 'REGISTRIES'
            logLevel = org.slf4j.event.Level.DEBUG
        }
    }

    mods {
        "${mod_id}" {
            sourceSet(sourceSets.main)
        }
    }
}

sourceSets.main.resources {
    srcDir 'src/generated/resources'
    exclude '.cache'
}
configurations {
    runtimeClasspath.extendsFrom localRuntime
}

dependencies {
    implementation "curse.maven:agritech-evolved-1287394:9155589"

    testImplementation platform("org.junit:junit-bom:5.13.4")
    testImplementation "org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter"
    testRuntimeOnly "org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher"
}

var generateModMetadata = tasks.register("generateModMetadata", ProcessResources) {
    var replaceProperties = [
            minecraft_version      : minecraft_version,
            minecraft_version_range: minecraft_version_range,
            neo_version            : neo_version,
            loader_version_range   : loader_version_range,
            mod_id                 : mod_id,
            mod_name               : mod_name,
            mod_license            : mod_license,
            mod_version            : mod_version,
    ]
    inputs.properties replaceProperties
    expand replaceProperties
    from "src/main/templates"
    into "build/generated/sources/modMetadata"
}
sourceSets.main.resources.srcDir generateModMetadata
neoForge.ideSyncTask generateModMetadata

tasks.named('test') {

}

tasks.named('jar') {

}

tasks.withType(JavaCompile).configureEach {

}

idea {

        downloadSources = true
        downloadJavadoc = true
    }

    runs {
        client {
            client()
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id

            server()
            programArgument '--nogui'
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

            type = "gameTestServer"
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        data {
            clientData()
            programArguments.addAll '--mod', project.mod_id, '--all', '--output', file('src/generated/resources/').getAbsolutePath(), '--existing', file('src/main/resources/').getAbsolutePath()
            systemProperty 'neoforge.enabledGameTestNamespaces', project.mod_id
        }

        configureEach {
            systemProperty 'forge.logging.markers', 'REGISTRIES'
            logLevel = org.slf4j.event.Level.DEBUG
        }
    }

    mods {

            sourceSet(sourceSets.main)
        }
    }
}

}

sourceSets.main.resources.srcDir generateModMetadata

tasks.withType(JavaCompile).configureEach {

1	# Modular Planters: design
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-28. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-10-28.
4	
5	Modular Planters is an addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). It lets a player replace dozens or hundreds of ATE Powered Planters with a few multiblocks, while each one produces, draws and costs about what the same number of Powered Planters would.
6	
7	Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner. The brainstorm record, with the research behind these numbers, is `NOTES.md` in the mod folder.
8	
9	## Why
10	
11	The owner's farm runs about 400 ATE Powered Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds. 333 of them grow nickel for a reactor fuel line, each with 2 MK3 Speed Modules, insanium farmland and a cloche. Those nickel seeds are maxed in every Productive Farming trait (see "Seed traits"). Every planter needs its own seed, soil, two modules and a Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Adding capacity means placing and configuring one more planter and one more node each time.
12	
13	The mod collapses this into a few multiblocks. A planter block holding 64 seeds stands in for 64 Powered Planters. One connection to the multiblock's core replaces the per-planter nodes.
14	
15	## Goals
16	
17	- A planter block with N growing seeds produces what N Powered Planters with the same seed, soil, modules and fertilizer produce, and draws the same power.
18	- A fully upgraded planter block costs about what 64 upgraded Powered Planters cost.
19	- One connection to the core (an LN node, a cable, pipes, or the ME block) runs a whole multiblock.
20	- Planter blocks that can't be reached in a build can still be managed from the core's screen.
21	- It works in any modpack: it follows the pack's ATE config and recipes, and its own recipes are datapack recipes a pack can replace.
22	
23	## Non-goals
24	
25	- No new crops, soils, fertilizers or upgrade items. The mod uses ATE's own Speed and Yield Modules and ATE's own planter recipes.
26	- No dedicated Logistics Networks block. An ordinary LN node on the core does the job.
27	- NeoForge on Minecraft 26.1.2 only. No Fabric and no other Minecraft versions.
28	- No 3D scenes in the guide. Oracle Index doesn't support them, so example builds are still images.
29	
30	## Anti-goals
31	
32	These would make the mod a failure even if it worked:
33	
34	- A planter block out-producing the matching number of Powered Planters, apart from the built-in cloche's yield rule below.
35	- Voiding items. When there's nowhere to put outputs, planter blocks wait.
36	- Requiring AE2, Applied Flux or Logistics Networks. All three are optional.
37	- Hard-coding ATE's default numbers. In game, every ATE number is read from ATE's live config.
38	- Copying code from ModularBees. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0 and this mod is MIT, so ModularBees may be read for ideas only.

62	| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy is kept. |
63	| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer, shared by every planter block. |
64	| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |

75	  - **Fertilizer in:** items inserted into the core go to the fertilizer blocks. Only fertilizers are accepted.
76	  - **Outputs:** items extracted from the core come out of the export blocks.

78	- **While not formed**, the core exposes no capabilities (my call).

145	## How a planter block grows
146	
147	### Contents
148	
149	The planter block's screen has four slots, all filled by hand. They can also be filled from the core's screen.
150	
151	| Slot | Holds |
152	|---|---|
153	| Seed | A seed bin: up to 64 seeds of one item type. Anything a Powered Planter accepts, saplings included. See "Seed traits". |
154	| Soil | One soil type, up to 64. Anything in ATE's `agritechevolved:soil_modifiers` data map, including Mystical Agradditions cruxes. |
155	| Module 1 | One ATE module type (Speed or Yield, MK1 to MK3), up to 64. |
156	| Module 2 | Same as module 1. |
157	
158	- There's no fertilizer slot and there are no output slots. Fertilizer comes from the fertilizer blocks, and outputs go to the export blocks or ME.
159	
160	### Seed traits
161	
162	Other mods can change a seed through ATE's planter events. Productive Farming, which FTB Evolution 2 includes, gives seeds traits such as Growth and Yield. Each harvest can raise one trait, and ATE writes the changed seed back into the planter. Seeds whose traits differ don't stack. The owner chose that every seed in a planter block keeps its own traits, so a planter block matches the same number of Powered Planters exactly:
163	
164	- **What the bin holds:** up to 64 seeds of one item type, each kept as its own stack of 1 with its own data. Seeds of the same item with different traits can go in together. Players moving from Powered Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them.
165	- **How the slot looks:** on screen the bin looks like one slot showing the seed and the count. Hovering over it lists how many seeds have each trait combination (my call).
166	- **Bin order:** seeds stay in the order they were put in (my call). The seed numbering below follows that order.
167	- **Taking seeds out:** the builder decides how seeds are taken back out of the bin.
168	- **Each seed levels on its own,** exactly as it would in its own Powered Planter.
169	- **No Productive Farming code:** all of this works through ATE's events, so Productive Farming isn't a dependency.
170	- The seed and soil must be a valid pair under ATE's planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`). The mod reads those recipes, so new ATE crops and KubeJS recipes work without changes.
171	
172	### Seeds, soil and modules
173	
174	- **Growing seeds:** G = the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. 64 seeds on 13 soil grow the first 13 in bin order. The other 51 are idle, and the screen says so.
175	- **One module covers one seed.** Let A = the smaller of module 1's count and G, and B = the smaller of module 2's count and G. Number the growing seeds 1 to G. Seed i gets module 1 if i is at most A, and module 2 if i is at most B. So by modules the seeds fall into at most three sets:
176	  - The smaller of A and B: seeds with both modules.
177	  - The larger minus the smaller: seeds with only the fuller slot's module.
178	  - G minus the larger: seeds with no module.
179	- **Groups:** a group is a set of growing seeds with the same module set and identical seed data, traits included. Seeds with different traits are in different groups even when they have the same modules.
180	- **Why seeds pair up this way (my call):** it matches a player filling Powered Planters one at a time with both modules before starting the next.
181	- **The screen shows coverage:** "23/64 seeds upgraded" when modules run short, and "13 working, 51 idle" when soil runs short.
182	
183	### Growth
184	
185	Each group behaves exactly like that many Powered Planters with that module set, running in lockstep:
186	
187	- **Progress:** each group keeps its own progress counter.
188	- **Growth time:** recomputed every tick with ATE's formula: `max(1, round(advanced base processing time / (soil x module speed x fertilizer speed x cloche speed)))`.
189	  - Module speed uses ATE's speed module multipliers and yield module speed penalties, as in `AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.getModuleSpeedModifier`.
190	  - Cloche speed is ATE's configured cloche speed bonus.
191	  - The planter block then fires ATE's `PlanterProcessingTimeEvent` once for the group, passing itself as the planter and one of the group's seeds. Every seed in a group has identical data, so one event speaks for all of them. The planter block uses whatever time the event returns. That's how Productive Farming's Growth trait applies.
192	- **Harvest:** when a group's progress reaches its growth time, the whole group harvests at once.
193	- **After a harvest,** seeds whose traits just changed form new groups. Every seed that harvested starts again at zero, so no progress is lost or gained.
194	
195	### Power
196	
197	- **Draw per tick:** for each group still growing, the number of seeds times `round(base power consumption x module power multiplier)`. Only Speed Modules raise power, as in ATE's `getModulePowerModifier`.
198	- **When there isn't enough:** if the power blocks can't cover the planter block's full draw for a tick, no group in that planter block advances that tick. A planter block never runs only some of its seeds.
199	- **Who gets power first (my call):** planter blocks draw in a fixed order, sorted by block position. When power runs short, the same planter blocks keep running and the rest pause, so it doesn't flicker between them.
200	- **Waiting to harvest:** a group that's ready to harvest but waiting for output room draws no power, as in ATE.
201	
202	### Fertilizer
203	
204	Each growing seed uses fertilizer at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so N seeds use what N Powered Planters would.
205	
206	- **Which fertilizer (my call):** the fertilizer used is the item in the first non-empty slot of the fertilizer blocks, taken in a fixed order.
207	- **When a group counts as fertilized (my call, revised 2026-10-29 after the final review):** each tick, the fertilizer stored is a budget shared by every planter block of the core. Planter blocks claim from it in the same position order as power, and each group claims as many items as it has seeds, all or nothing. A group that claims is fertilized for that tick. A group that can't claim runs unfertilized that tick, so one stack can't speed up more seeds than it could pay for. A fertilized group uses the fertilizer's speed and yield multipliers from ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map, and consumes one item per seed when it harvests. Otherwise the group runs unfertilized.
208	- **No fertilizer block:** if there's no fertilizer block, or it's empty, every planter block runs unfertilized.
209	
210	### Harvest and outputs
211	
212	When a group harvests, each seed in it goes through the same steps, in the same order as ATE's Powered Planter (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584):
213	
214	1. Fire `PlanterPreHarvestEvent` for that seed, passing the planter block as the planter. Write the seed the event returns back into that seed's place in the bin. This is where Productive Farming raises a trait.
215	2. Roll that seed's drops from ATE's recipe, including chance drops, using the seed the event returned.
216	3. Apply ATE's yield rounding to each drop. This is r in "Built-in cloche".
217	4. Fire `PlanterPostHarvestEvent` for that seed with its own drop list. Productive Farming adds its Yield bonus to each stack in that list, so each seed must get its own event and its own list.
218	5. Add the cloche's kept fraction for each drop to the planter block's remainders. Extra items from the remainders are added after the event, never into the event's list, so per-stack bonuses from other mods never apply to them.
219	6. Insert the drops into ME, if there's an online ME block, and then into the export blocks.
220	7. Consume one fertilizer for that seed, if the group is fertilized.
221	
222	Output room (my call):
223	
224	- A group only starts harvesting if the export blocks, plus ME if it's online, have room for the group's drops as ATE's recipe lists them. This is like ATE's `hasOutputSpace`.
225	- Other mods can add to the drops during the events, so they may still not all fit. Whatever doesn't fit is held inside the planter block, and the planter block pauses until all of it has been moved out.
226	- Nothing is voided.
227	
228	### Built-in cloche
229	
230	The built-in cloche is always on and uses ATE's configured cloche speed and yield bonuses. They're 1.15 and 1.10 by default.
231	
232	**Speed:** the cloche speed bonus goes into the growth time formula above.
233	
234	**Yield:** ATE's Powered Planter gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x module yield x cloche yield))` for each drop. For a 1-item drop at 1.1 that rounds back to 1, so the cloche's yield bonus does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away. The owner decided this; it's the mod's one deliberate buff.
235	
236	The exact rule (my call, written so that it never gives less than ATE and never adds more than the cloche's own share):
237	
238	1. For each drop, let x = count x fertilizer yield x module yield, and e = x x cloche yield.
239	2. ATE's result is r = max(1, round(e)). The player always gets at least r.
240	3. The fraction kept is the smaller of (e - r) and x x (cloche yield - 1), or 0 if e - r is negative.
241	4. Add the kept fraction to a running remainder for that item, saved per planter block. Each time the remainder reaches 1, give one extra item and subtract 1.
242	
243	The yield bonus from other mods, such as Productive Farming's Yield trait, is added after this rule and never counts toward x or e.
244	
245	With the default 1.1 and a 1-item drop, each seed gets one extra every tenth harvest, a 10% gain. With a Yield MK3 (2.0), e is 2.2 and r is 2, so the cloche adds 0.2 per drop, again 10%. It also applies to seeds and fertilized essence, the same way ATE's yield bonus does (my call).
246	
247	### Changing contents mid-growth
248	
249	The builder decides how progress is kept when a player changes seeds, soil or modules mid-growth. The rule is that no change can produce a harvest earlier or larger than the same change to Powered Planters would. Changing the seed or soil type resets progress, as in ATE.
250

316	
317	These are shaped crafting recipes, shipped as datapack JSON so packs can replace them. The owner chose each key ingredient. The other ingredients and the grid patterns are my calls.
318	
319	| Block | Pattern | Key |
320	|---|---|---|
321	| Frame | `PPP` `PIP` `PPP` | P = ATE Powered Planter (`agritechevolved:advanced_planter`), I = block of iron |
322	| Planter | `FFF` `FIF` `FFF` | F = Frame, I = ATE Infused Farmland (`agritechevolved:infused_farmland`) |
323	| Core | `IGI` `GCG` `IDI` | C = ATE Cloche Dome (`agritechevolved:cloche_dome`), G = glass (`#c:glass_blocks`), I = block of iron, D = block of diamond |
324	| Power | `IRI` `RCR` `IRI` | C = ATE Capacitor Tier 3 (`agritechevolved:capacitor_tier3`), R = block of redstone, I = block of iron |
325	| Fertilizer | `IBI` `BSB` `IBI` | S = ATE Fertilizer Spreader (`agritechevolved:fertilizer_spreader`), B = bone block, I = block of iron |
326	| Export | `IHI` `HSH` `IHI` | S = ATE Silo (`agritechevolved:silo`), H = hopper, I = block of iron |
327	| ME | `IFI` `FXF` `IFI` | X = ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), F = fluix crystal (`#c:gems/fluix`), I = block of iron. Has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`. |

329	The owner's reasoning:
330	
331	- **Progression:** a player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game, when they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite.
332	- **Gating:** the power block carries the progression gate. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor takes diamonds and emeralds.
333	- **Two-step planter block:** it takes 64 Powered Planters, and splitting that into two steps keeps any one recipe from needing stacks of an item.
334	- **Following the pack:** using Powered Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. Players can also break existing Powered Planters and craft them straight in.
335	- **Iron for the frame:** a frame used as filler costs 8 Powered Planters, and an iron center keeps it from also costing 9 diamonds.
336	- **No frames in the other parts:** they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Powered Planters to each.

395	- **Manual play** in the FTB Evolution 2 instance, including a Logistics Networks node on the core and an ME block with Applied Flux.
396	
397	## Left to the builder
398	
399	- **Build setup:** the Gradle setup, the NeoForge and Java versions within the constraints above, and the code structure.
400	- **Multiblock mechanics:** how forming and re-checking are triggered, and how the structure behaves across chunk borders and unloaded chunks. Whatever happens, items must never be lost or duplicated.
401	- **NeoForge 26.1 APIs:** how the doorway and part capabilities are wired with the transfer API that ATE already uses (`ResourceHandler<ItemResource>`, `ItemStacksResourceHandler`).
402	- **Screens:** the menu, screen and network code for the core screen and remote opening.
403	- **AE2 and Applied Flux:** how the ME block uses their APIs. ModularBees' `xmod/ae/` and the Applied Flux jar are references, read but not copied.
404	- **Changing contents mid-growth:** the exact progress rule, within the rule stated above. Seeds added mid-growth must not join a group's progress.
405	- **The seed bin:** how players take seeds back out of it.
406	- **Assets:** how the textures are edited, and how the guide's images are made.
407	
408	## Calls made without the owner
409	
410	These are listed together so the owner can check them:
411	
412	1. Parts:
413	   - several power blocks and several fertilizer blocks pool their contents, and several export blocks fill one after another;
414	   - the power block buffer is 4,000,000 RF, the fertilizer block has 27 slots, and the export block has 54.
415	2. Energy:
416	   - the power block accepts energy as fast as the multiblock can use it;
417	   - energy can't be extracted from it;
418	   - it keeps its energy when broken.
419	3. Structure rules:
420	   - the core exposes nothing while not formed;
421	   - frames count toward the cap, and the cap is in the server config;
422	   - a second ME block or a second core stops the multiblock from forming.
423	4. The ME block:
424	   - it moves export contents into ME every 20 ticks;
425	   - it tops fertilizer up every 20 ticks from one chosen fertilizer;
426	   - with Applied Flux, it refills only what was used.
427	5. Module coverage pairs both modules on the same seeds first.
428	6. Power: planter blocks are powered in a fixed order by position.
429	7. Fertilizer:
430	   - the first fertilizer found in the fertilizer blocks is the one used;
431	   - a group counts as fertilized only when there's enough for all its seeds.
432	8. Seed bin:
433	   - seeds keep the order they were put in;
434	   - hovering over the bin lists the trait combinations.
435	9. The exact cloche yield rule, applying it to every drop, and adding its extras after the post-harvest event.
436	10. Output room: a group starts harvesting when there's room for its listed drops, and anything other mods add that doesn't fit is held in the planter block until it's moved out.
437	11. Recipes: every ingredient and pattern other than the key ingredients.
438	12. Looks:
439	    - full cube blocks with no crop rendering;
440	    - an on and off texture for the planter block.
441	13. An optional Jade plugin, and no JEI plugin.
442	14. The server config contents.

# Modular Planters: design

Date: 2026-10-28. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-10-28.

Modular Planters is an addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). It lets a player replace dozens or hundreds of ATE Powered Planters with a few multiblocks, while each one produces, draws and costs about what the same number of Powered Planters would.

Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner. The brainstorm record, with the research behind these numbers, is `NOTES.md` in the mod folder.

## Why

The owner's farm runs about 400 ATE Powered Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds. 333 of them grow nickel for a reactor fuel line, each with 2 MK3 Speed Modules, insanium farmland and a cloche. Those nickel seeds are maxed in every Productive Farming trait (see "Seed traits"). Every planter needs its own seed, soil, two modules and a Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Adding capacity means placing and configuring one more planter and one more node each time.

The mod collapses this into a few multiblocks. A planter block holding 64 seeds stands in for 64 Powered Planters. One connection to the multiblock's core replaces the per-planter nodes.

## Goals

- A planter block with N growing seeds produces what N Powered Planters with the same seed, soil, modules and fertilizer produce, and draws the same power.
- A fully upgraded planter block costs about what 64 upgraded Powered Planters cost.
- One connection to the core (an LN node, a cable, pipes, or the ME block) runs a whole multiblock.
- Planter blocks that can't be reached in a build can still be managed from the core's screen.
- It works in any modpack: it follows the pack's ATE config and recipes, and its own recipes are datapack recipes a pack can replace.

## Non-goals

- No new crops, soils, fertilizers or upgrade items. The mod uses ATE's own Speed and Yield Modules and ATE's own planter recipes.
- No dedicated Logistics Networks block. An ordinary LN node on the core does the job.
- NeoForge on Minecraft 26.1.2 only. No Fabric and no other Minecraft versions.
- No 3D scenes in the guide. Oracle Index doesn't support them, so example builds are still images.

## Anti-goals

These would make the mod a failure even if it worked:

- A planter block out-producing the matching number of Powered Planters, apart from the built-in cloche's yield rule below.
- Voiding items. When there's nowhere to put outputs, planter blocks wait.
- Requiring AE2, Applied Flux or Logistics Networks. All three are optional.
- Hard-coding ATE's default numbers. In game, every ATE number is read from ATE's live config.
- Copying code from ModularBees. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0 and this mod is MIT, so ModularBees may be read for ideas only.

## Constraints

- **Platform:** NeoForge, Minecraft 26.1.2. It must run in the FTB Evolution 2 instance (pack 1.5.1, NeoForge 26.1.2.121) at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`.
- **Dependencies:**
  - Hard: ATE (tested with 2.2.0.6).
  - Optional: AE2 (26.1.13-beta), Applied Flux (26.1-1.0.2), Logistics Networks (26.1.2-1.13.0), Oracle Index (2.0.0), Jade.
  - The mod has to load and work with any combination of the optional ones missing.
- **Identity:**
  - Mod name: Modular Planters.
  - Mod id: `modular_planters`.
  - Java package: `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
  - GitHub repo: `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`.
  - Local folder: `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`, renamed from `ate-planter-multiblock` (my call).
- **License:** MIT, with every line of code written for this mod. Textures are adapted from ATE's, which are MIT, so ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.
- **ATE config:** every ATE number is read through ATE's public static getters in `com.misterd.agritechevolved.Config`, for example `Config.getPlanterBasePowerConsumption()`, the same way the Powered Planter reads them. ATE's defaults appear in this document only as worked examples. Tests may pin those defaults.
- **Logistics Networks tags:** no block in this mod may be in LN's blacklist tags (`logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants).

## The blocks

| Block | Job |
|---|---|
| Core | Forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche, opens the core screen, and acts as a doorway for energy, fertilizer and outputs. Stores nothing itself. |
| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy is kept. |
| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer, shared by every planter block. |
| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
| ME | Optional, and only exists when AE2 is installed. Connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. |
| Frame | Does nothing except connect parts. |

There's no import block. The fertilizer block covers that job.

### Core

- **It's a doorway.** While formed, the core exposes three capabilities:
  - **Energy:** energy inserted into the core goes to the power blocks.
  - **Fertilizer in:** items inserted into the core go to the fertilizer blocks. Only fertilizers are accepted.
  - **Outputs:** items extracted from the core come out of the export blocks.
  - So one LN node on the core with the owner's existing three-channel settings runs a whole multiblock. Each part block also exposes its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.
- **While not formed**, the core exposes no capabilities (my call).
- **It applies the built-in cloche to every planter block.** The cloche is always on and needs no item. See "Built-in cloche".
- **Its screen** is described under "Core screen".

### Power block

- Stores energy. Several power blocks pool their storage (my call).
- Buffer: 4,000,000 RF each, the same as ATE's Capacitor Tier 3, which is its key recipe ingredient (my call). This is set in the mod's server config.
- Accepts energy at least as fast as the whole multiblock can draw it, with no low per-tick limit (my call). ATE's Tier 3 Capacitor moves only 8,192 RF/t, which wouldn't cover even one full planter block.
- Energy can't be extracted from it (my call).
- When broken, it keeps its stored energy in the dropped item, like ATE's capacitors (my call).

### Fertilizer block

- 27 slots (my call). Accepts only items in ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map.
- Several fertilizer blocks pool their contents (my call).
- Drops its contents when broken.

### Export block

- 54 slots (my call). Only the multiblock can insert. Anything can extract.
- Several export blocks fill one after another (my call).
- Drops its contents when broken.

### Planter block

The planter block's own behavior is described under "How a planter block grows".

### ME block

- Only exists when AE2 is installed: the block's registration, item and recipe are all conditional on AE2.
- It's an AE2 grid node that uses one channel. A multiblock can have at most one. A second ME block keeps the multiblock from forming, since it would do nothing (my call).
- **Outputs:**
  - Harvested outputs go straight into ME storage.
  - Whatever ME doesn't accept goes into the export blocks.
  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block also moves whatever is in the export blocks into ME (my call).
- **Fertilizer:**
  - The ME block's screen has one filter slot where the player picks a fertilizer.
  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block tops the fertilizer blocks up with that fertilizer from ME (my call).
- **Applied Flux:**
  - When Applied Flux is also installed, the ME block keeps the power blocks charged from the network's stored FE.
  - Each tick it draws only enough to refill what the power blocks used. It doesn't fill them ahead of time (my call).
  - Without Applied Flux, power comes in through the core or the power blocks.
  - A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works either way, with no code in this mod.

### Frame block

- Connects parts and does nothing else.
- It's also the in-between step when crafting a planter block (see "Recipes").

## Structure

- **Free form.** The multiblock is the core plus every part block connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't connect.
- **Size cap:** at most 24 parts, not counting the core. Frames count (my call).
  - Above the cap, the multiblock doesn't form, and the core's screen says why.
  - The cap is in the server config, default 24 (my call).
- **Required parts:** at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
- **Two cores:** if the connected parts reach a second core, neither forms. The core's screen names the problem block and its position (my call).
- **Re-checking:** the core re-checks the shape when a part next to the structure is placed or broken.
- **When the shape breaks:** the planter blocks stop, but every block keeps its contents.

The guide shows three example builds from the brainstorm, saved in `mockups/layouts.html`. They're examples only, since any connected shape works:

- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed and a 3x3 glass canopy.
- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor and floors of planter blocks above it.
- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the other parts take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks extend outward in four arms.

## How a planter block grows

### Contents

The planter block's screen has four slots, all filled by hand. They can also be filled from the core's screen.

| Slot | Holds |
|---|---|
| Seed | A seed bin: up to 64 seeds of one item type. Anything a Powered Planter accepts, saplings included. See "Seed traits". |
| Soil | One soil type, up to 64. Anything in ATE's `agritechevolved:soil_modifiers` data map, including Mystical Agradditions cruxes. |
| Module 1 | One ATE module type (Speed or Yield, MK1 to MK3), up to 64. |
| Module 2 | Same as module 1. |

- There's no fertilizer slot and there are no output slots. Fertilizer comes from the fertilizer blocks, and outputs go to the export blocks or ME.

### Seed traits

Other mods can change a seed through ATE's planter events. Productive Farming, which FTB Evolution 2 includes, gives seeds traits such as Growth and Yield. Each harvest can raise one trait, and ATE writes the changed seed back into the planter. Seeds whose traits differ don't stack. The owner chose that every seed in a planter block keeps its own traits, so a planter block matches the same number of Powered Planters exactly:

- **What the bin holds:** up to 64 seeds of one item type, each kept as its own stack of 1 with its own data. Seeds of the same item with different traits can go in together. Players moving from Powered Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them.
- **How the slot looks:** on screen the bin looks like one slot showing the seed and the count. Hovering over it lists how many seeds have each trait combination (my call).
- **Bin order:** seeds stay in the order they were put in (my call). The seed numbering below follows that order.
- **Taking seeds out:** the builder decides how seeds are taken back out of the bin.
- **Each seed levels on its own,** exactly as it would in its own Powered Planter.
- **No Productive Farming code:** all of this works through ATE's events, so Productive Farming isn't a dependency.
- The seed and soil must be a valid pair under ATE's planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`). The mod reads those recipes, so new ATE crops and KubeJS recipes work without changes.

### Seeds, soil and modules

- **Growing seeds:** G = the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. 64 seeds on 13 soil grow the first 13 in bin order. The other 51 are idle, and the screen says so.
- **One module covers one seed.** Let A = the smaller of module 1's count and G, and B = the smaller of module 2's count and G. Number the growing seeds 1 to G. Seed i gets module 1 if i is at most A, and module 2 if i is at most B. So by modules the seeds fall into at most three sets:
  - The smaller of A and B: seeds with both modules.
  - The larger minus the smaller: seeds with only the fuller slot's module.
  - G minus the larger: seeds with no module.
- **Groups:** a group is a set of growing seeds with the same module set and identical seed data, traits included. Seeds with different traits are in different groups even when they have the same modules.
- **Why seeds pair up this way (my call):** it matches a player filling Powered Planters one at a time with both modules before starting the next.
- **The screen shows coverage:** "23/64 seeds upgraded" when modules run short, and "13 working, 51 idle" when soil runs short.

### Growth

Each group behaves exactly like that many Powered Planters with that module set, running in lockstep:

- **Progress:** each group keeps its own progress counter.
- **Growth time:** recomputed every tick with ATE's formula: `max(1, round(advanced base processing time / (soil x module speed x fertilizer speed x cloche speed)))`.
  - Module speed uses ATE's speed module multipliers and yield module speed penalties, as in `AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.getModuleSpeedModifier`.
  - Cloche speed is ATE's configured cloche speed bonus.
  - The planter block then fires ATE's `PlanterProcessingTimeEvent` once for the group, passing itself as the planter and one of the group's seeds. Every seed in a group has identical data, so one event speaks for all of them. The planter block uses whatever time the event returns. That's how Productive Farming's Growth trait applies.
- **Harvest:** when a group's progress reaches its growth time, the whole group harvests at once.
- **After a harvest,** seeds whose traits just changed form new groups. Every seed that harvested starts again at zero, so no progress is lost or gained.

### Power

- **Draw per tick:** for each group still growing, the number of seeds times `round(base power consumption x module power multiplier)`. Only Speed Modules raise power, as in ATE's `getModulePowerModifier`.
- **When there isn't enough:** if the power blocks can't cover the planter block's full draw for a tick, no group in that planter block advances that tick. A planter block never runs only some of its seeds.
- **Who gets power first (my call):** planter blocks draw in a fixed order, sorted by block position. When power runs short, the same planter blocks keep running and the rest pause, so it doesn't flicker between them.
- **Waiting to harvest:** a group that's ready to harvest but waiting for output room draws no power, as in ATE.

### Fertilizer

Each growing seed uses fertilizer at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so N seeds use what N Powered Planters would.

- **Which fertilizer (my call):** the fertilizer used is the item in the first non-empty slot of the fertilizer blocks, taken in a fixed order.
- **When a group counts as fertilized (my call, revised 2026-10-29 after the final review):** each tick, the fertilizer stored is a budget shared by every planter block of the core. Planter blocks claim from it in the same position order as power, and each group claims as many items as it has seeds, all or nothing. A group that claims is fertilized for that tick. A group that can't claim runs unfertilized that tick, so one stack can't speed up more seeds than it could pay for. A fertilized group uses the fertilizer's speed and yield multipliers from ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map, and consumes one item per seed when it harvests. Otherwise the group runs unfertilized.
- **No fertilizer block:** if there's no fertilizer block, or it's empty, every planter block runs unfertilized.

### Harvest and outputs

When a group harvests, each seed in it goes through the same steps, in the same order as ATE's Powered Planter (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584):

1. Fire `PlanterPreHarvestEvent` for that seed, passing the planter block as the planter. Write the seed the event returns back into that seed's place in the bin. This is where Productive Farming raises a trait.
2. Roll that seed's drops from ATE's recipe, including chance drops, using the seed the event returned.
3. Apply ATE's yield rounding to each drop. This is r in "Built-in cloche".
4. Fire `PlanterPostHarvestEvent` for that seed with its own drop list. Productive Farming adds its Yield bonus to each stack in that list, so each seed must get its own event and its own list.
5. Add the cloche's kept fraction for each drop to the planter block's remainders. Extra items from the remainders are added after the event, never into the event's list, so per-stack bonuses from other mods never apply to them.
6. Insert the drops into ME, if there's an online ME block, and then into the export blocks.
7. Consume one fertilizer for that seed, if the group is fertilized.

Output room (my call):

- A group only starts harvesting if the export blocks, plus ME if it's online, have room for the group's drops as ATE's recipe lists them. This is like ATE's `hasOutputSpace`.
- Other mods can add to the drops during the events, so they may still not all fit. Whatever doesn't fit is held inside the planter block, and the planter block pauses until all of it has been moved out.
- Nothing is voided.

### Built-in cloche

The built-in cloche is always on and uses ATE's configured cloche speed and yield bonuses. They're 1.15 and 1.10 by default.

**Speed:** the cloche speed bonus goes into the growth time formula above.

**Yield:** ATE's Powered Planter gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x module yield x cloche yield))` for each drop. For a 1-item drop at 1.1 that rounds back to 1, so the cloche's yield bonus does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away. The owner decided this; it's the mod's one deliberate buff.

The exact rule (my call, written so that it never gives less than ATE and never adds more than the cloche's own share):

1. For each drop, let x = count x fertilizer yield x module yield, and e = x x cloche yield.
2. ATE's result is r = max(1, round(e)). The player always gets at least r.
3. The fraction kept is the smaller of (e - r) and x x (cloche yield - 1), or 0 if e - r is negative.
4. Add the kept fraction to a running remainder for that item, saved per planter block. Each time the remainder reaches 1, give one extra item and subtract 1.

The yield bonus from other mods, such as Productive Farming's Yield trait, is added after this rule and never counts toward x or e.

With the default 1.1 and a 1-item drop, each seed gets one extra every tenth harvest, a 10% gain. With a Yield MK3 (2.0), e is 2.2 and r is 2, so the cloche adds 0.2 per drop, again 10%. It also applies to seeds and fertilized essence, the same way ATE's yield bonus does (my call).

### Changing contents mid-growth

The builder decides how progress is kept when a player changes seeds, soil or modules mid-growth. The rule is that no change can produce a harvest earlier or larger than the same change to Powered Planters would. Changing the seed or soil type resets progress, as in ATE.

## Core screen

The owner approved the layout in `mockups/core-screen.html`. It's modeled on the Logistics Networks Computer's Node Table (`LogisticsNetworks/src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`).

- **Top bar:**
  - Formed state and part count, for example "FORMED 18 / 24".
  - When the multiblock isn't formed, the reason, naming the problem block and its position if there is one.
- **Totals:** stored power and current draw, fertilizer stored, how full the export blocks are, and ME status.
- **Planter table:**
  - One row per planter block, grouped by seed type under collapsible headings, the way LN groups nodes by label.
  - Each row shows:
    - the seed;
    - how many seeds are growing;
    - module coverage;
    - a status: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle;
    - the block's position.
- **Row buttons:**
  - **Outline** toggles a glowing outline on that planter block in the world, visible only to that player, like LN's lamp button.
  - **Open** opens that planter block's screen remotely. It's the same screen as in the world, with a "Back to core" button added.
- **Rules:**
  - The table updates live.
  - Opening a planter block remotely is checked on the server: the player must be in range of the core, and the planter block must belong to that core's formed multiblock.

## Integrations

### Logistics Networks

- There's no LN code in the mod. A node on the core works through the core's doorway capabilities.
- The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node uses its best upgrade for every channel, and LN's default limits are:

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items a second |
|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 5,120 |
| Netherite | about 2.1 billion RF | 200,000 |

- Example with ATE's defaults: a full planter block of 64 nickel seeds with 2 MK3 Speed Modules, insanium farmland and the built-in cloche.
  - **Power:** it draws 32,768 RF/t whatever the seeds' traits.
  - **Items:** with seeds that have no traits, it puts out about 24 items a second. With seeds maxed in Productive Farming's Growth and Yield, like the owner's, it puts out about 320 items a second. That's more than a gold upgrade moves.
  - **Upgrade needed:** a diamond upgrade covers up to 7 such planter blocks, and power is the limit. More than 7 needs a netherite upgrade, or more nodes on the power blocks.
- The guide has to include this table and example.

### AE2 and Applied Flux

See the ME block above. AE2 and Applied Flux are compile-time-only dependencies. All code that touches them sits behind a mod-loaded check, so the mod loads without them.

### Productive Farming

- There's no Productive Farming code in the mod. Its traits work through ATE's three planter events, fired as described under "How a planter block grows".
- It's in FTB Evolution 2, with `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, so Mystical Agriculture seeds gain traits there. Manual testing uses that pack.

### Jade

An optional Jade plugin (my call, the lowest priority in the mod):

- On the core: formed state.
- On a planter block: growing seeds and status.

### JEI

No JEI plugin. The crafting recipes show up in JEI on their own, and the crops are ATE's own planter recipes, which ATE already shows.

## Recipes

These are shaped crafting recipes, shipped as datapack JSON so packs can replace them. The owner chose each key ingredient. The other ingredients and the grid patterns are my calls.

| Block | Pattern | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | `PPP` `PIP` `PPP` | P = ATE Powered Planter (`agritechevolved:advanced_planter`), I = block of iron |
| Planter | `FFF` `FIF` `FFF` | F = Frame, I = ATE Infused Farmland (`agritechevolved:infused_farmland`) |
| Core | `IGI` `GCG` `IDI` | C = ATE Cloche Dome (`agritechevolved:cloche_dome`), G = glass (`#c:glass_blocks`), I = block of iron, D = block of diamond |
| Power | `IRI` `RCR` `IRI` | C = ATE Capacitor Tier 3 (`agritechevolved:capacitor_tier3`), R = block of redstone, I = block of iron |
| Fertilizer | `IBI` `BSB` `IBI` | S = ATE Fertilizer Spreader (`agritechevolved:fertilizer_spreader`), B = bone block, I = block of iron |
| Export | `IHI` `HSH` `IHI` | S = ATE Silo (`agritechevolved:silo`), H = hopper, I = block of iron |
| ME | `IFI` `FXF` `IFI` | X = ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), F = fluix crystal (`#c:gems/fluix`), I = block of iron. Has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`. |

The owner's reasoning:

- **Progression:** a player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game, when they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite.
- **Gating:** the power block carries the progression gate. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor takes diamonds and emeralds.
- **Two-step planter block:** it takes 64 Powered Planters, and splitting that into two steps keeps any one recipe from needing stacks of an item.
- **Following the pack:** using Powered Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. Players can also break existing Powered Planters and craft them straight in.
- **Iron for the frame:** a frame used as filler costs 8 Powered Planters, and an iron center keeps it from also costing 9 diamonds.
- **No frames in the other parts:** they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Powered Planters to each.

## Textures and models

- Every block is a full cube (my call).
- Textures are adapted from ATE's, in `AgritechEvolved/src/main/resources/assets/agritechevolved/textures/block/`, so the blocks look like part of ATE. For example:
  - the power block from the capacitor textures;
  - the core from the cloche dome textures;
  - the planter block from the planter textures.
- Planter blocks don't render their crops (my call). A planter block can switch between an "on" and an "off" texture while growing, the way ATE's capacitors do (my call).

## Server config

The mod's own server config holds (my call):

- the part cap (default 24);
- the power block's buffer (default 4,000,000 RF);
- the ME block's export and fertilizer interval (default 20 ticks).

ATE's numbers are never copied into this config. They're always read from ATE.

## Guide

The guide is an Oracle Index book, set up the way Oritech does it:

- The pages live in a `wiki/` folder, using the moddedmc.wiki layout.
- `processResources` copies them into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters`.
- Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it isn't needed at runtime.

Pages:

- An overview.
- One page per block, with its recipe.
- The building rules.
- The three example builds as still images.
- The planter block's seed, soil and module rules.
- The built-in cloche rule.
- The Logistics Networks upgrade table and example.
- AE2 and Applied Flux.

  - grouping seeds by module coverage;
  - the soil limit;
  - growth time and power draw per group;
  - fertilizer use;
  - the cloche yield rule.
  - One test checks that a planter block with N seeds gives the same expected output and power as N simulated Powered Planters, using ATE's default numbers.
  - One test registers a listener on ATE's three events that acts like Productive Farming: it changes the seed and adds a flat bonus to each drop stack. The test checks that seeds level on their own, that each seed gets its own post-harvest event, and that the cloche's extra items never get the bonus.
- **NeoForge GameTests** for the world behavior:

  - missing required parts;

11. Recipes: every ingredient and pattern other than the key ingredients.
12. Looks:

## Decisions

All of these were agreed in the 2026-10-28 sessions.

### Scope

- The mod is called Modular Planters. You checked CurseForge and found no clashing names.
  - Mod id `modular_planters`, Java package `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
  - GitHub repo `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`, cloned at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters` next to your Hostile-Neural-Networks fork. That location is my call: your CLAUDE.md says personal code goes in `~/code`, but that folder doesn't exist.
- A public mod for other players, with its source code on GitHub.
- MIT license, like ATE. All of the code is written for this mod. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0, so it's used only to see how a multiblock core links its parts and how its ME block talks to AE2. None of its code is copied in.
- NeoForge only, Minecraft 26.1.2.
- Hard dependency on ATE. Optional dependencies on Applied Energistics 2 (AE2), Applied Flux and Logistics Networks.
- In game, the mod reads ATE's live config, the same way a Powered Planter does. When a modpack changes ATE's numbers, a planter block still matches that pack's own Powered Planters. ATE's default config is used only for the planning math in these notes and for the tests. Settled on 2026-10-28 in the second session, from what was open question 6.
- Tests that verify the logic, plus manual play in the FTB Evolution 2 instance.
- Guide written for Oracle Index, the way Oritech does it.

### Block lineup

| Block | Job |
|---|---|
| Core | Forms the multiblock and owns the built-in cloche. Stores nothing itself. |
| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy lives, so the multiblock can't run without one. |
| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer and accepts it from pipes, LN or AE2. Shared by every planter block. |
| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
| ME (optional, needs AE2) | Joins an AE2 network. Sends outputs into ME storage and keeps the fertilizer block stocked. |
| Frame | Does nothing except link parts together. |

There's no separate import block. The fertilizer block took its only job.

The core is a doorway: energy sent into it goes to the power blocks, fertilizer goes to the fertilizer blocks, and outputs come out of the export blocks. That's what lets one LN node on the core run a whole multiblock with your current three-channel settings, as long as the node has an upgrade big enough for the multiblock (see Integrations). Each block also accepts its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.

### Planter block

- Holds one seed type up to 64, soil or crux up to 64, and two module slots that hold up to 64 each. You fill all of these by hand in the planter block's screen.
- **Seed traits:** every seed keeps its own Productive Farming traits, so seeds of one type with different traits can go in together and each one levels on its own, the same as 64 Powered Planters (you chose this, option a). ATE's harvest events fire once per seed, each with that seed's own drops. Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum: Growth 3, Yield 3, Resistance 4 and Mutability 4 (`TraitsHelper.TRAIT_VALUES`).
- The number of seeds that actually grow is the smaller of seeds and soil. 64 seeds on 13 insanium farmland grow 13, and the screen says so.
- Accepts anything an ATE Powered Planter accepts, saplings included. It reads ATE's own planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`), so new ATE crops and KubeJS-added recipes work without changes.
- **Fertilizer:** each growing seed uses it at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so 64 seeds use what 64 planters would. If the fertilizer block is empty, or there isn't one, the planter blocks run unfertilized.
- **Power:** each seed draws what one Powered Planter with the same modules draws. If the multiblock can't cover a planter block's full draw for a tick, that block pauses. It doesn't run part of its seeds.
- **Outputs** go into the export blocks. When they're full, planter blocks pause until there's room. Nothing is voided.

....
### Built-in cloche

- Always on. It uses ATE's configured cloche speed bonus, 1.15 by default.
- Yield change: ATE multiplies each drop count by the yield bonus and rounds to the nearest whole number, so a 1-item drop at 1.1 rounds back to 1 and the cloche's yield does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction instead: its configured yield bonus builds up a remainder on each harvest. With the default 1.1, a single-item drop gets one extra every tenth harvest. That's a 10% gain, never more than one extra item at a time.

### Structure

The structure is free form:

- The multiblock is the core plus every part touching it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't count.
- Cap of 24 parts, not counting the core. Above that it doesn't form, and the core says why.
- It needs at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
- The core re-checks the shape when a part is placed or broken. If the shape breaks, the planter blocks stop but keep their contents.

The guide shows three of the layouts from the session as example builds (see `mockups/layouts.html`):

- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed layer, and a 3x3 glass canopy. The bed center and canopy center can't be clicked, so they take frame or glass.
- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor, floors of planter blocks above it and a glass roof.
- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the IO blocks take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks grow outward as four arms.

### Integrations

- **Logistics Networks: no dedicated block.** The block first proposed would mostly have been a rebuilt LN node. One node on the core does the same job, keeps your copy and paste workflow, and puts no LN code in the mod.
  - The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node without upgrades moves only 2,000 RF/t and 0.8 items a second, while one full planter block of the nickel setup draws 32,768 RF/t and puts out about 22 items a second.
  - A node uses the best upgrade in any of its slots for every channel. So one diamond upgrade covers up to 250,000 RF/t and 5,120 items a second, which is enough for 7 full planter blocks of the nickel setup. Above 7, the node needs a netherite upgrade.
  - The alternative to a netherite upgrade is more nodes, since each power block also accepts energy directly.
  - The guide needs to tell players this, with the numbers for each upgrade.
- **AE2: one ME block.** It sends outputs into ME storage the moment they're harvested, and keeps the fertilizer block stocked with a fertilizer you choose from ME. A block beats buses because the fuel line note flags import buses slowing to one pull every 40 ticks, and nickel alone makes about 5,300 essence a minute plus seeds and fertilized essence.
- **Applied Flux: optional, used by the ME block.** Plain AE2 doesn't carry FE, but Applied Flux lets an ME network store and deliver it. Applied Flux is installed in FTB Evolution 2, but not in ATM11. When both AE2 and Applied Flux are installed, the ME block also keeps the power blocks charged from the network's FE, so one ME connection runs power, fertilizer and outputs. Without Applied Flux the ME block handles only items and fertilizer, and power comes in through the core or the power blocks as usual. A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works, with no code in this mod.

## Defaults I picked
....
### ModularBees

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularBees`. It's NeoForge 26.1.2.59-beta, LGPL-3.0 license, package `com.glodblock.github.modularbees`.

- Multiblock base: `common/tileentities/base/TileMBModularCore.java`. It holds a `refresh` flag, `formStructure()`, `buildStructure()` returning a `TryResult` with a message and position, and `logicTick()` that only runs while formed. Parts extend `TileMBModularComponent` and link to one core. `util/StructureListener` watches for block changes.
- The centrifuge shape is in `TileModularCentrifuge.getPoses()`: 3x3 layers at core y-1 (corners only), y and y+1. Any centrifuge part fits any slot, with at most one heater. The beehive is a fixed 3x3x3.
- The import block (`TileCentrifugeImport`) pulls from the container it faces every `AUTO_IMPORT_INTERVAL`.
- Recipes are in `datagen/MBRecipeProvider.java`. The plain beehive part block (`modular_beehive_part`) is cheap: 8 scented planks around iron bars. Every other beehive part, such as the export, feeder, treater and overclocker, has a part block as one of its ingredients.
- The ME export block's recipe (`me_beehive_export.json`) is an ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), 2 fluix crystals, 2 iron bars and a modular export block. It has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`, so it only exists when AE2 is installed.
- AE2 integration lives in `xmod/ae/`. `TileMEExport` extends `TileAENetworkHost`, inserts with `AEItemKey`, has a 12-slot filter with a whitelist toggle, and pushes every `ME_EXPORT_INTERVAL`. The core collects parts that implement `MEExportAction` and calls `sendToMENetwork`.

### Applied Flux

The installed jar is `AppliedFlux-26.1-1.0.2-neoforge.jar`, by GlodBlock, who also wrote ModularBees. Its package is `com.glodblock.github.appflux`.

- It comes as a block (`TileFluxAccessor`) and as a cable part (`PartFluxAccessor`). Both join the AE2 grid.
- It has an input/output mode, blocked sides, a fast mode, and an `EnergyDistributeService` that pushes FE into neighbors' energy storage (`distribute`).
- It's in FTB Evolution 2 but not ATM11, which has no Applied Flux and no Flux Networks.

### Logistics Networks

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/LogisticsNetworks`.

- A node sticks onto one block and has 9 channels. It moves items, fluids, FE and Mekanism chemicals, and works with any block that exposes those capabilities.
- Tags `logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants stop nodes or transfers. The mod must not end up in them.
- Upgrade limits are in `upgrade/UpgradeLimitsConfig.java` (`defaultForTier`), and a server can change them in its config. A node's tier is the best upgrade in any of its slots (`NodeUpgradeData.getUpgradeTier`). Energy channels run every tick no matter the tier (`TransferEngine.cooldownRemaining`). Item channels run once every "min ticks".

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items per run | Min ticks between item runs | Items a second |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 16 | 20 | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 32 | 10 | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 64 | 5 | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 256 | 1 | 5,120 |
| Netherite | 2,147,483,647 RF | 10,000 | 1 | 200,000 |

- One full planter block of the nickel setup harvests 1,024 times a minute. That's 1,024 essence, about 205 seeds and about 102 fertilized essence, so about 22 items a second, or about 24 with the built-in cloche.
- With your maxed nickel seeds, one full planter block puts out about 310 items a second, or about 319 with the built-in cloche (see "Productive Farming seed traits"). That's more than a gold upgrade's 256, so even one planter block needs a diamond upgrade. Diamond moves enough items for about 16 such planter blocks, but its 250,000 RF/t covers only 7.
- The Computer block's Node Table is the model for the core's screen. Its guide page is `src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`. Each row shows the block's icon and name, its dimension and coordinates, a lamp button that outlines the node in the world, and a gear button that opens the node's screen remotely. Labeled nodes are grouped under collapsible headers, and the remote screen has a "Back to table" button.

### Productive Farming seed traits

The design document's reviewer found this, and I checked it on 2026-10-28.

- Productive Farming 0.13.0 (`productivefarming-26.1.2-0.13.0.jar`) is installed in FTB Evolution 2. Its repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/productivefarming`, branch `origin/dev-26.1`.
- `integrations/agritech/AgriTechEvolvedEventHandler.java` listens to all three ATE planter events:
  - **`PlanterProcessingTimeEvent`:** divides growth time by (Growth level + 1).
  - **`PlanterPreHarvestEvent`:** each harvest may raise one random trait on the planted seed. ATE writes the changed seed back into the seed slot (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584).
  - **`PlanterPostHarvestEvent`:** adds the Yield level to every drop stack that isn't a seed, and copies the traits onto dropped seeds (`AgriTechStatsHelper.applyStats`). It adds to each stack, not each item, so the event has to see one stack per seed for 64 seeds to get 64 times the bonus.
- The traits are Growth and Yield (0 to 3), and Resistance and Mutability (0 to 4). Seeds whose traits differ don't stack.
- The pack's `config/productivefarming-server.toml` sets `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, and PF's `external_seeds` tag includes `#mysticalagriculture:seeds`. So Mystical Agriculture seeds in ATE planters gain traits.
- Nickel is in `productivefarming:mystical_tier_4`, and `data_maps/item/stat_increase_chance.json` gives that tier 0.03. That's a 3% chance per harvest to raise one trait.
- Maxed Growth 3 and Yield 3 make a planter 4 times as fast with 4 essence per harvest, so about 16 times the essence.
- **Decision:** every seed keeps its own traits (option a). The design document's "Seed traits" section has the details.

Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum. These numbers are calculated from the code and that statement, not measured in game:

- **Growth:** the 75-tick harvest becomes `max(1, round(75 / 4))` = 19 ticks, about 63.2 harvests a minute instead of 16.
- **Essence:** 1 + 3 = 4 per harvest, so about 252.6 essence a minute per planter. The built-in cloche adds 0.1 a harvest, about 258.9.
- **Other drops:** fertilized essence gets the Yield bonus too, 0.4 a harvest. Seeds don't, 0.2 a harvest.
- **Power:** unchanged at 512 RF/t a planter, since traits don't change power per tick.
- **The reactor:** the fuel line needs 5,313 nickel essence a minute. The fuel line note sized 333 planters at 16 essence a minute each, with no traits. At about 252.6 each, 22 maxed planters cover it, or 21 with the built-in cloche.
- **What 333 maxed planters make:** about 84,000 essence a minute, about 16 times what the reactor burns. If the farm in game makes about 5,300 a minute instead, one of these readings is wrong, and the design's per-seed events depend on it.

### Oracle Index, as Oritech uses it

The Oracle Index repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index`, and Oritech's is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech`.

- Pages use the moddedmc.wiki layout: a `wiki/` folder with `sinytra-wiki.json` (id, platforms, owners), `docs/` and `content/` folders, `_meta.json` files for ordering, and `.mdx` pages with front matter (`id`, `type`, `title`).
- Oritech copies `wiki/` into `assets/oracle_index/books/oritech` in `processResources`, leaving out `assets/item/**`. Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it's optional at runtime.
- Oritech uses the `org.moddedmc.wiki.toolkit` Gradle plugin, plus the wiki exporter (`wiki-exporter.json`, a `wikiExport` run config) to render item images.
- Supported page components: markdown, crafting recipes, images (assets), callouts, audio and video embeds. There are no 3D or rotatable scenes like AE2's GameScenes, so the example builds will be still images.

### Test instance: FTB Evolution 2

The instance is at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`. It runs pack version 1.5.1 with NeoForge 26.1.2.121, ZGC and an 8 GB heap.

Relevant mods already installed:

- `agritechevolved-2.2.0.6+neoforge-mc26.1.2`
- `appliedenergistics2-26.1.13-beta`
- `AppliedFlux-26.1-1.0.2-neoforge`
- `logisticsnetworks-26.1.2-1.13.0`
- `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0`
- `oritech-2.0.0-exp12`
- `MysticalAgriculture-26.1.2-9.0.10`
- `productivefarming-26.1.2-0.13.0`
- `MysticalAgradditions-26.1.2-9.0.4`
- `jei-26.1.2-neoforge-29.47.0.111`
- `Jade-mc26.1-NeoForge-26.1.12`

ModularBees is not in this instance.

- Cap of 24 parts, not counting the core. Above that it doesn't form, and the core says why.
- It needs at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
- The core re-checks the shape when a part is placed or broken. If the shape breaks, the planter blocks stop but keep their contents.

The guide shows three of the layouts from the session as example builds (see `mockups/layouts.html`):

- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed layer, and a 3x3 glass canopy. The bed center and canopy center can't be clicked, so they take frame or glass.
- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor, floors of planter blocks above it and a glass roof.
- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the IO blocks take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks grow outward as four arms.

### Integrations

- **Logistics Networks: no dedicated block.** The block first proposed would mostly have been a rebuilt LN node. One node on the core does the same job, keeps your copy and paste workflow, and puts no LN code in the mod.
  - The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node without upgrades moves only 2,000 RF/t and 0.8 items a second, while one full planter block of the nickel setup draws 32,768 RF/t and puts out about 22 items a second.
  - A node uses the best upgrade in any of its slots for every channel. So one diamond upgrade covers up to 250,000 RF/t and 5,120 items a second, which is enough for 7 full planter blocks of the nickel setup. Above 7, the node needs a netherite upgrade.
  - The alternative to a netherite upgrade is more nodes, since each power block also accepts energy directly.
  - The guide needs to tell players this, with the numbers for each upgrade.
- **AE2: one ME block.** It sends outputs into ME storage the moment they're harvested, and keeps the fertilizer block stocked with a fertilizer you choose from ME. A block beats buses because the fuel line note flags import buses slowing to one pull every 40 ticks, and nickel alone makes about 5,300 essence a minute plus seeds and fertilized essence.
- **Applied Flux: optional, used by the ME block.** Plain AE2 doesn't carry FE, but Applied Flux lets an ME network store and deliver it. Applied Flux is installed in FTB Evolution 2, but not in ATM11. When both AE2 and Applied Flux are installed, the ME block also keeps the power blocks charged from the network's FE, so one ME connection runs power, fertilizer and outputs. Without Applied Flux the ME block handles only items and fertilizer, and power comes in through the core or the power blocks as usual. A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works, with no code in this mod.

## Defaults I picked
....
### ModularBees

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularBees`. It's NeoForge 26.1.2.59-beta, LGPL-3.0 license, package `com.glodblock.github.modularbees`.

- Multiblock base: `common/tileentities/base/TileMBModularCore.java`. It holds a `refresh` flag, `formStructure()`, `buildStructure()` returning a `TryResult` with a message and position, and `logicTick()` that only runs while formed. Parts extend `TileMBModularComponent` and link to one core. `util/StructureListener` watches for block changes.
- The centrifuge shape is in `TileModularCentrifuge.getPoses()`: 3x3 layers at core y-1 (corners only), y and y+1. Any centrifuge part fits any slot, with at most one heater. The beehive is a fixed 3x3x3.
- The import block (`TileCentrifugeImport`) pulls from the container it faces every `AUTO_IMPORT_INTERVAL`.
- Recipes are in `datagen/MBRecipeProvider.java`. The plain beehive part block (`modular_beehive_part`) is cheap: 8 scented planks around iron bars. Every other beehive part, such as the export, feeder, treater and overclocker, has a part block as one of its ingredients.
- The ME export block's recipe (`me_beehive_export.json`) is an ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), 2 fluix crystals, 2 iron bars and a modular export block. It has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`, so it only exists when AE2 is installed.
- AE2 integration lives in `xmod/ae/`. `TileMEExport` extends `TileAENetworkHost`, inserts with `AEItemKey`, has a 12-slot filter with a whitelist toggle, and pushes every `ME_EXPORT_INTERVAL`. The core collects parts that implement `MEExportAction` and calls `sendToMENetwork`.

### Applied Flux

The installed jar is `AppliedFlux-26.1-1.0.2-neoforge.jar`, by GlodBlock, who also wrote ModularBees. Its package is `com.glodblock.github.appflux`.

- It comes as a block (`TileFluxAccessor`) and as a cable part (`PartFluxAccessor`). Both join the AE2 grid.
- It has an input/output mode, blocked sides, a fast mode, and an `EnergyDistributeService` that pushes FE into neighbors' energy storage (`distribute`).
- It's in FTB Evolution 2 but not ATM11, which has no Applied Flux and no Flux Networks.

### Logistics Networks

The repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/LogisticsNetworks`.

- A node sticks onto one block and has 9 channels. It moves items, fluids, FE and Mekanism chemicals, and works with any block that exposes those capabilities.
- Tags `logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants stop nodes or transfers. The mod must not end up in them.
- Upgrade limits are in `upgrade/UpgradeLimitsConfig.java` (`defaultForTier`), and a server can change them in its config. A node's tier is the best upgrade in any of its slots (`NodeUpgradeData.getUpgradeTier`). Energy channels run every tick no matter the tier (`TransferEngine.cooldownRemaining`). Item channels run once every "min ticks".

| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items per run | Min ticks between item runs | Items a second |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | 2,000 RF | 16 | 20 | 0.8 |
| Iron | 10,000 RF | 32 | 10 | 64 |
| Gold | 50,000 RF | 64 | 5 | 256 |
| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 256 | 1 | 5,120 |
| Netherite | 2,147,483,647 RF | 10,000 | 1 | 200,000 |

- One full planter block of the nickel setup harvests 1,024 times a minute. That's 1,024 essence, about 205 seeds and about 102 fertilized essence, so about 22 items a second, or about 24 with the built-in cloche.
- With your maxed nickel seeds, one full planter block puts out about 310 items a second, or about 319 with the built-in cloche (see "Productive Farming seed traits"). That's more than a gold upgrade's 256, so even one planter block needs a diamond upgrade. Diamond moves enough items for about 16 such planter blocks, but its 250,000 RF/t covers only 7.
- The Computer block's Node Table is the model for the core's screen. Its guide page is `src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`. Each row shows the block's icon and name, its dimension and coordinates, a lamp button that outlines the node in the world, and a gear button that opens the node's screen remotely. Labeled nodes are grouped under collapsible headers, and the remote screen has a "Back to table" button.

### Productive Farming seed traits

The design document's reviewer found this, and I checked it on 2026-10-28.

- Productive Farming 0.13.0 (`productivefarming-26.1.2-0.13.0.jar`) is installed in FTB Evolution 2. Its repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/productivefarming`, branch `origin/dev-26.1`.
- `integrations/agritech/AgriTechEvolvedEventHandler.java` listens to all three ATE planter events:
  - **`PlanterProcessingTimeEvent`:** divides growth time by (Growth level + 1).
  - **`PlanterPreHarvestEvent`:** each harvest may raise one random trait on the planted seed. ATE writes the changed seed back into the seed slot (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584).
  - **`PlanterPostHarvestEvent`:** adds the Yield level to every drop stack that isn't a seed, and copies the traits onto dropped seeds (`AgriTechStatsHelper.applyStats`). It adds to each stack, not each item, so the event has to see one stack per seed for 64 seeds to get 64 times the bonus.
- The traits are Growth and Yield (0 to 3), and Resistance and Mutability (0 to 4). Seeds whose traits differ don't stack.
- The pack's `config/productivefarming-server.toml` sets `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, and PF's `external_seeds` tag includes `#mysticalagriculture:seeds`. So Mystical Agriculture seeds in ATE planters gain traits.
- Nickel is in `productivefarming:mystical_tier_4`, and `data_maps/item/stat_increase_chance.json` gives that tier 0.03. That's a 3% chance per harvest to raise one trait.
- Maxed Growth 3 and Yield 3 make a planter 4 times as fast with 4 essence per harvest, so about 16 times the essence.
- **Decision:** every seed keeps its own traits (option a). The design document's "Seed traits" section has the details.

Your nickel seeds are Very High in every trait, which is the maximum. These numbers are calculated from the code and that statement, not measured in game:

- **Growth:** the 75-tick harvest becomes `max(1, round(75 / 4))` = 19 ticks, about 63.2 harvests a minute instead of 16.
- **Essence:** 1 + 3 = 4 per harvest, so about 252.6 essence a minute per planter. The built-in cloche adds 0.1 a harvest, about 258.9.
- **Other drops:** fertilized essence gets the Yield bonus too, 0.4 a harvest. Seeds don't, 0.2 a harvest.
- **Power:** unchanged at 512 RF/t a planter, since traits don't change power per tick.
- **The reactor:** the fuel line needs 5,313 nickel essence a minute. The fuel line note sized 333 planters at 16 essence a minute each, with no traits. At about 252.6 each, 22 maxed planters cover it, or 21 with the built-in cloche.
- **What 333 maxed planters make:** about 84,000 essence a minute, about 16 times what the reactor burns. If the farm in game makes about 5,300 a minute instead, one of these readings is wrong, and the design's per-seed events depend on it.

### Oracle Index, as Oritech uses it

The Oracle Index repo is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index`, and Oritech's is at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech`.

- Pages use the moddedmc.wiki layout: a `wiki/` folder with `sinytra-wiki.json` (id, platforms, owners), `docs/` and `content/` folders, `_meta.json` files for ordering, and `.mdx` pages with front matter (`id`, `type`, `title`).
- Oritech copies `wiki/` into `assets/oracle_index/books/oritech` in `processResources`, leaving out `assets/item/**`. Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it's optional at runtime.
- Oritech uses the `org.moddedmc.wiki.toolkit` Gradle plugin, plus the wiki exporter (`wiki-exporter.json`, a `wikiExport` run config) to render item images.
- Supported page components: markdown, crafting recipes, images (assets), callouts, audio and video embeds. There are no 3D or rotatable scenes like AE2's GameScenes, so the example builds will be still images.

### Test instance: FTB Evolution 2

The instance is at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`. It runs pack version 1.5.1 with NeoForge 26.1.2.121, ZGC and an 8 GB heap.

Relevant mods already installed:

- `agritechevolved-2.2.0.6+neoforge-mc26.1.2`
- `appliedenergistics2-26.1.13-beta`
- `AppliedFlux-26.1-1.0.2-neoforge`
- `logisticsnetworks-26.1.2-1.13.0`
- `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0`
- `oritech-2.0.0-exp12`
- `MysticalAgriculture-26.1.2-9.0.10`
- `productivefarming-26.1.2-0.13.0`
- `MysticalAgradditions-26.1.2-9.0.4`
- `jei-26.1.2-neoforge-29.47.0.111`

ModularBees is not in this instance.
